source.title: Sleep Spindles Preferentially Consolidate Weakly Encoded Memories

confidence_rationale: The cleanest counter-evidence to the Q-055 erosion hypothesis, and in humans: across wake, weak memories decay fastest, but a nap ATTENUATES that effect until forgetting rates are equalised across encoding strengths, with fast spindle density predicting the rescue of weak items specifically. If sleep selectively protects the weak/under-represented traces, its net effect on a diverse population would be DIVERSITY-PRESERVING, not winner-take-all. Confidence 0.70: strong human design with a physiological correlate, but it measures declarative word-pair retention, not behavioural trajectory diversity, so the mapping is by analogy.
failure_signatures: Contradicts a naive winner-take-all reading of sleep replay: sleep preferentially rescues WEAK traces rather than amplifying strong ones, so the net population-level effect can equalise rather than concentrate.

Effect is specific to weak items (spindles did not correlate with intermediate or strong item memory), so sleep's protective action is targeted at exactly the traces a diversity-erosion account predicts would be lost.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Compared with wake, sleep attenuates the rapid forgetting of weakly encoded memories until forgetting rates are equivalent across encoding strengths; fast sleep-spindle density (especially spindles coupled to slow oscillations) selectively predicts consolidation of the weak items.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct support for the Q-055 diversity-PRESERVING arm. If SD-017 sleep preferentially protects weak / low-frequency trajectory classes -- the very ones a Hebbian winner-take-all account (MECH-120) predicts would be eroded -- then sleep is plausibly a NET POSITIVE for ARC-065 behavioural diversity, equalising rather than concentrating the trajectory-class distribution.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is declarative episodic memory (word pairs) in humans, not procedural/behavioural trajectory diversity. 'Weak memory' (low encoding strength) maps only loosely onto 'low-frequency / under-committed trajectory class'. The mechanism (spindle-SO coupling) protecting weak traces is suggestive but its applicability to REE's replay substrate is an inference, not a demonstration.
mapping.source_context: Human nap study, n=54 (36 nap / 18 wake), word-pair associative memory at three encoding strengths; PSG with spindle/SO analysis.

confidence_components.notes: Robust human design with a clear physiological mediator (Stickgold group). Mapping fidelity moderate (declarative-memory-strength proxy for behavioural-diversity). This is the load-bearing entry for the 'sleep preserves diversity' position.
